Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 series in September as usual this fall, but this year's launch event will echo several unusual aspects of how iPhones were rolled out during the 2020 COVID pandemic.

How this fall's iPhone launch will differ from Apple's previous launch patterns

Apple has many highly successful products, but the iPhone remains its flagship, accounting for a large share of the company's overall revenue.

It is therefore understandable that Apple is committed to maintaining stability around iPhone launches. By keeping the timing of new iPhone releases predictable, Apple is better able to satisfy Wall Street and its customers.

Generally, Apple announces new iPhones in early September—usually four new models—and all of them go on sale in late September.

But 2020 was an unusual year because of the COVID pandemic.

The fall 2020 iPhone lineup was not announced until October, and only two of the new models went on sale at launch, with the remaining two delayed until November.

Rumors this year suggest Apple's launch plans will once again see similar irregularities.

While the expectation of a September event remains unchanged, Apple may not put all new iPhone models on sale at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models may be available for purchase initially: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to be unveiled in September, but rumors suggest its release date could be pushed back slightly, possibly going on sale a few weeks after the Pro models.

Apple may also break with tradition on the total number of iPhone models.

If rumors that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will be pushed back to spring 2027 prove accurate, only three new models will debut this fall—the smallest fall iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether driven by strategic considerations or by a global memory chip shortage and the challenges of mass-producing an entirely new foldable phone, Apple's fall 2026 event could reprise several features of its 2020 launch.

What new features would you like to see at this fall's iPhone launch event? Let us know in the comments.
